Rewrite the following expression as the sum of a perfect square and a constant.

$({y}^{2}+9y+\frac{81}{4})+2=(y\,\,+$
{{field-1}} $)^{2}+$
{{field-2}}
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{y}^{2}+2ay+{a}^{2}=(y+a)^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+9y+\frac{81}{4} & = \\ {y}^{2}+9y+{(\frac{9}{2})}^{2} & = \\ {y}^{2}+2\cdot \frac{9}{2}y+{(\frac{9}{2})}^{2} & = \\ {(y+\frac{9}{2})}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}^{2}+9y+\frac{81}{4})+2 & = \\ {(y+\frac{9}{2})}^{2}+2 & .\end{aligned}
$$
